content:
Apple's first foldable iPhone is expected to debut in just over a week. Reports indicate that during development, Apple internally considered launching a brand-new Apple Pencil designed specifically for the iPhone Ultra, though this stylus is almost certainly never going to actually hit the market.

The information comes from Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, who specifically emphasised that this Apple Pencil will not be announced next month. Nevertheless, he still detailed the original design appearance and expected operation of this stylus.

This stylus was originally different from the Apple Pencil currently used with the iPad series; its design is shorter to match the shorter body proportions of the iPhone Ultra. However, similar to the iPad version of the Apple Pencil, it was originally designed to attach magnetically to the side of the device for easy storage and charging.

He pointed out that holding this stylus while using the iPhone Ultra would be quite awkward, because the stylus attaches to the side of the device; by contrast, when using an iPad, when you operate the device in landscape mode, the stylus attaches to the top.

He also mentioned that this stylus would very likely leave "unsightly marks" on the more fragile inner screen of the iPhone Ultra.

He ultimately speculated that the main reason Apple decided not to release this stylus is that it did not want to go against the position Steve Jobs insisted upon when unveiling the original iPhone—"Who wants a stylus?"

I personally still think an Apple Pencil designed specifically for the iPhone Ultra would be quite useful, but it seems we won't be seeing this stylus for the time being.

After the most recent round of price increases, it might be worth keeping an eye on Apple's refurbished product store—you just might find a bargain, as refurbished products of all kinds can save quite a bit, including iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, and Apple TV.
